headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist by default; broad egress in opik plus file uploads and API-driven workflows in plane create unsafe pairwise coupling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: opik can ingest REST API content and has broad network egress, while plane accepts file uploads and hyperlinks. A shared or copied artifact from plane could be treated as trusted input by opik, creating an injection path. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF plane content is copied into opik prompts or evaluation inputs without sanitization
IF opik treats uploaded or API-fetched content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data separator in the handoff
Strip markup and executable directives from plane exports before ingestion
Use a read-only review step for any copied content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between plane and opik

B_data_leakage.rationale: plane touches files, images, notes, and hyperlinks and supports file uploads; opik has broad network egress. If plane-managed content is forwarded into opik workflows, sensitive workspace material can leave the local boundary. The profiles do not show direct shared storage, so this is not high, but the leakage path is plausible in default API-driven use.
conditions: IF plane file uploads or notes are forwarded into opik API calls
IF either agent is configured to process sensitive workspace content
mitigations: Restrict opik inputs to redacted excerpts
Disable forwarding of plane attachments by default
Review outbound destinations for opik API traffic
Tag sensitive plane items and block export
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on the handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: opik exposes REST API calls and broad egress, while plane supports multiple instances and file uploads but no filesystem write capability is listed. There is no documented shared mutable resource or overlapping write surface, so direct conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because the pair is unverified, but the available profiles do not show a strong write collision.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external API resource
IF an operator manually synchronizes state between plane and opik without locking
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials per agent
Avoid shared mutable targets
Serialize manual updates through one operator
Document ownership of each workspace object

D_cascading_error.rationale: plane manages issues, tasks, and roadmaps, so its outputs are likely to be acted on downstream. opik can consume API-fed content and broad egress, making it plausible that one agent’s output becomes the other’s input without verification. That creates a default cascade risk, though the profiles do not prove autonomous action-taking.
conditions: IF opik-generated summaries are imported into plane as authoritative task content
IF plane actions are triggered from opik outputs without human verification
mitigations: Require human approval before creating or updating plane items
Add a verification checklist for opik-derived claims
Keep source links attached to every imported summary
Use a separate review queue for cross-agent outputs
requires-engineering: add confidence/provenance gating

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and the profiles do not show PHI, EU residency, or certification mismatches. plane documents file uploads and support channels, while opik shows broad egress, but no specific regulated data class is identified. With no concrete residency or retention conflict, compliance risk is limited and only becomes relevant under regulated-data deployment.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed through both agents
IF deployment policies require residency or retention guarantees not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Review retention settings before enabling uploads
Document data-flow boundaries
Use separate environments for regulated and non-regulated work
